text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — customer support flagged a few incidents where requests hit 503s when the primary model (llama-70b) is saturated. Proposal: automatic variant swap to a quantized/compatible variant (e.g. llama-70b-q4) instead of returning 503. Thoughts?

Samir Patel: +1 to avoiding 503s. We need a clear policy though: capacity threshold, tier awareness, and a circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation.

Anika Rao: Strong caution: enterprise customers might expect no silent quality regressions. We should make auto-swap opt-out per-customer and show active fallbacks in the console.

Liam O'Neill: KV-cache impact is the big one — swapping models often invalidates caches and can spike latency. We should prefer variants that share tokenizer and architecture to keep cache hits.

Eva K.: Agreed. In practice we should rank variants by compatibility: same-arch/quantized > architecture-compatible > different-arch. Also prefer variants with similar context length.

Samir Patel: Draft routing pseudocode:
```
if primary.util >= THRESHOLD and route.auto_fallback_enabled:
  for v in sorted_variants_by(policy_rank):
    if v.available and v.util < SOFT_LIMIT:
      route.to(v)
      emit_event("fallback.triggered", {from: primary, to: v, reason: "capacity"})
      break
  else:
    return 503
```
Policy knobs: THRESHOLD (e.g. 0.85), SOFT_LIMIT (0.75), max_fallbacks_per_minute, opt_out flag per-customer.

Maya Chen: Good start. Questions: how do we handle paid tiers? For enterprise we might prefer a higher-quality fallback even if more expensive. For free tier, prefer cheaper variants.

Anika Rao: Exactly — routing policy should be tier-scoped. Example rules:
- enterprise: prefer same-arch high-accuracy quant variant, keep latency SLOs, notify customer.
- standard: prefer smaller high-throughput variant.
- free: cheapest compatible variant.
Make these editable in console as rule sets.

Liam O'Neill: Also think about cascading fallbacks across regions. If us-west primary saturated and we route to another region's variant, we need cross-region latency checks and capacity quotas. Might be better to failover within region first.

Eva K.: Telemetry needs to capture: fallback.count, fallback.latency_penalty, fallback.quality_regression_signal (from eval hooks), fallback.cost_delta. We should emit a structured event so billing/console can show per-customer impact.

Samir Patel: Example event shape (for analytics):
```
fallback.triggered: {
  customer_id, primary_model, fallback_model, tier, region, reason: "capacity", timestamp, tokens_routed, cost_delta
}
```
We can stash these in observability with sampling for high-volume customers.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: feature-flag "auto_variant_fallback_v1" targeting 5% of traffic in staging -> canary.

Maya Chen: OK action items:
- Samir/Eng runtime: implement capacity-threshold + soft-limit logic + circuit-breaker (PR draft).
- Liam/Infra: ensure cache compatibility checks and region-first preference implemented.
- Anika/Console PM: add a toggle + rule editor and a fallback timeline in per-customer view (show events and cost delta).
- Eva/Telemetry: define fallback metrics + tagging and add regression alert hooks.
- Rollout plan: start behind feature flag at 5% (deploy-bot), monitor fallback.rate and quality signals for 72h, then increase.

Anika Rao: Also add an opt-out API: `auto_variant_fallback: boolean` in customer config and an override header `X-Redwood-Fallback: none|prefer-cheap|prefer-same-arch`.

Samir Patel: One more caveat: billing. If fallback routes to a cheaper model, customers should still be billed for the actual model tokens used (and we should surface delta). Add a console note when a call used a fallback and cost/diff.

Maya Chen: Sounds like consensus. I'll create a RFC doc and link to this thread. For immediate safety, Samir: can you bump THRESHOLD to 0.9 for the canary so we only trigger under real pressure?

Samir Patel: Yep — will set THRESHOLD=0.9 for canary and attach logs for any fallback triggers.

Liam O'Neill: If we see oscillation, we should add decay window (e.g., don't fallback again to same variant for X minutes) and a token-based rate limiter on fallback events.

Eva K.: I'll add telemetry dashboards: fallback per minute, per-customer cost delta, and quality alerts tied to eval prompt sets. Will wire up regression alerts.

Maya Chen: Awesome. Thanks all. Follow-ups in the RFC and PRs. :thumbsup:
